course_intent: Introduce students to the breadth of classical AI subfields (agents, knowledge representation, logic, expert systems, NLP, fuzzy logic, and introductory ML/data science) at a conceptual level — students should leave able to explain what each area is for and how it fits into the AI landscape, not implement any specific algorithm or system in depth.
depth_bound: Recommendations stay at the conceptual / overview level grounded in the Russell & Norvig framing. Implementation walkthroughs, framework-specific tutorials (PyTorch, scikit-learn, spaCy code), formal proofs, mathematical deep dives (transformer attention math, optimization theory), and hands-on coding exercises are beyond the course's depth bound.
key_topics: Intelligent agents, PEAS framework, and task-environment properties
Knowledge representation (propositional logic, FOL, semantic networks, frames, production rules)
Ontologies and ontology engineering (Protégé, pizza ontology example)
Rule-based expert systems with forward and backward chaining
Classical NLP pipeline (lexical, syntactic, semantic, pragmatic analysis, parse trees, PSGs)
Type-1 fuzzy logic (membership functions, fuzzification/defuzzification, fuzzy rules)
Wumpus World as a knowledge-based agent example
Introductory machine learning concepts (supervised/unsupervised/reinforcement, regression vs classification)
Data science workflow (collection, preprocessing, EDA, evaluation metrics)
AI history, Turing test, and AI categorizations (ANI/AGI/ASI)
one_liner: Broad undergraduate AI survey rooted in the Russell & Norvig textbook, covering classical symbolic AI (agents, logic, KR, ontologies, expert systems, classical NLP, fuzzy logic) plus an introductory tour of ML and data science at a conceptual level — does NOT teach hands-on implementation, modern deep learning depth, transformer-era NLP internals, or framework-specific coding.
ambiguity_note: Survey course spanning symbolic AI through introductory ML and data science — no single specialization dominates, and ML/DS coverage is conceptual rather than hands-on.
